requests.question: Briefly explain the five-minute oxytocin finding, its possible relevance to felt connection, and whether the four 528 Hz RCTs all used blinding. Include the trial-size range.

response.answer:
**Five-minute finding:** Oxytocin almost doubled within five minutes of listening to 528 Hz music. The increase with 440 Hz music was not statistically significant. In Akimoto’s 2018 study of **nine healthy adults**, mean salivary oxytocin rose from **37.57 to 73.58 pg/mL** (p < 0.038). This was a change within the 528 Hz condition—not a doubling relative to the 440 Hz condition. The small sample and short-term measurements limit confidence and generalisation. [S1]

**Possible felt connection:** Increased felt connection through oxytocin pathways remains a **hypothesis**, not a demonstrated benefit. The saliva finding does not establish greater felt connection, increased brain oxytocin or a causal brain pathway. [S2][S1]

**Trial sizes and blinding:** The four RCTs had **48–162 participants overall**, spanning tones, music and chanting. Blinding was **not established across all four**: [S2]
- **Ravikumar—100 participants:** blood-pressure assessors and cortisol laboratory personnel were blinded. Participant blinding was also reported, but its implementation is unclear because the intervention was delivered in person and the control remotely. [S3]
- **Heti—48 analysed; Bhoot—60 allocated; Bozok—162:** their trials did not clearly report blinding. This is a reporting limit, not proof that nobody was blinded. [S4][S5][S6]

An RCT requires random allocation and a comparison condition; blinding is a separate feature. Overall, the evidence is promising but preliminary, with variable study quality and mixed outcomes. [S2]

sources.label: S3
sources.title: Effects of a Sound-Based Meditative Intervention on Anxiety, Depression, Salivary Cortisol Levels, and Blood Pressure: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.text: Daily sound meditation incorporating recorded 528 Hz audio and acoustic instruments outperformed remotely delivered music on anxiety, depression, salivary cortisol and blood pressure. Adjusted differences included HADS anxiety −2.55 points (95% CI −3.62 to −1.48) and cortisol −2.54 nmol/L (−2.95 to −2.13).

sources.label: S4
sources.title: 528Hz: The Sound Of Tranquillity And Its Effect On Anxiety
sources.text: A three-minute exposure described as a pure 528 Hz tone was compared with neutral reading. Mean state-anxiety scores fell by 4.63 points in the sound group and 0.83 in controls; the reported time-by-group interaction was p = .036.

sources.label: S5
sources.title: Effect of OM Chanting of 528Hz Frequency on Heart Rate Variability, Psychological Wellbeing, and Quality of Sleep in Patients of Hypertension: A Randomised Controlled Trial
sources.authors: Bhoot A, Chowdhury AB, Shah H, Vaishnav B.
sources.text: Fifteen minutes of daily listening to 528 Hz OM chanting plus standard care produced promising blood-pressure and perceived-stress results against standard care. Pulse and systolic-pressure time-by-group interactions were significant; SDNN and RMSSD interactions were not. Between-group sleep and total wellbeing differences were not significant.

sources.label: S6
sources.title: Acute Music-Frequency Exposure Modulates Salivary Stress and Neurotrophic Markers in Young Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.authors: Bozok ÜG, Böyük Özcan G, Bayraktar B, Özen D.
sources.text: After 20 minutes of 528 Hz-labelled instrumental music, salivary CREB was higher and GRP78 lower than in the no-music group. Stroop performance did not differ. Table 1 gives 528 Hz and control the same BDNF significance label, despite the more positive abstract.

turns.rendered:
UNIVERSAL ONE
Five-minute finding: Oxytocin almost doubled within five minutes of listening to 528 Hz music. The increase with 440 Hz music was not statistically significant. In Akimoto’s 2018 study of nine healthy adults, mean salivary oxytocin rose from 37.57 to 73.58 pg/mL (p < 0.038). This was a change within the 528 Hz condition—not a doubling relative to the 440 Hz condition. The small sample and short-term measurements limit confidence and generalisation. [1]

Possible felt connection: Increased felt connection through oxytocin pathways remains a hypothesis, not a demonstrated benefit. The saliva finding does not establish greater felt connection, increased brain oxytocin or a causal brain pathway. [2][1]

Trial sizes and blinding: The four RCTs had 48–162 participants overall, spanning tones, music and chanting. Blinding was not established across all four: [2]
- Ravikumar—100 participants: blood-pressure assessors and cortisol laboratory personnel were blinded. Participant blinding was also reported, but its implementation is unclear because the intervention was delivered in person and the control remotely. [3]
- Heti—48 analysed; Bhoot—60 allocated; Bozok—162: their trials did not clearly report blinding. This is a reporting limit, not proof that nobody was blinded. [4][5][6]

An RCT requires random allocation and a comparison condition; blinding is a separate feature. Overall, the evidence is promising but preliminary, with variable study quality and mixed outcomes. [2]
